reports.title: KKR & Co. Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results November 9, 2026

lines: In 2026, we expect to return more than $40 billion to our clients, exceeding our previous annual record by more than 50%.

desk.headline: Adjusted net income up 29% to $1.78/share, beat; record fee earnings; >$40bn to be returned to clients in 2026
results: Adjusted net income rose 29% to $1.65bn ($1.78 per share), a record, beating the $1.58 estimate; GAAP profit to shareholders was $1.12bn.
Fee related earnings climbed 27% to $1.32bn, helped by higher management fees ($1.20bn) and a jump in fee related performance revenues.
Assets under management reached $804bn (+11%); new capital raised was $25bn, down from $43bn a year earlier, and $146bn remains uninvested.
Insurance (Global Atlantic) operating earnings fell to $230m from $305m, including a $26m actuarial review charge.
KKR spent $567m buying back 6.2m shares since 30 June, added $500m to the buyback plan and kept the quarterly dividend at $0.195.

guidance.summary: No formal earnings guidance. KKR expects to return more than $40bn to fund clients in 2026, a record, and about $2.0bn of adjusted net income from the USI sale in Q4 if it closes.

items.metric: Adjusted net income from USI sale

points: Management stressed a second straight quarter of record fee, operating and adjusted earnings per share.
Monetisations are on track for a record year, with more than $40bn to be returned to clients.
Expected after-tax proceeds of roughly $3.3bn from the USI sale are earmarked for buybacks, strategic holdings and insurance.
AI-related exposure was put at about 1–2% of firm-wide assets, focused on investment-grade counterparties.
KKR plans to move to a one-share, one-vote structure by its next results call.

watch: Closing of the USI sale and the roughly $2.0bn Q4 boost to adjusted net income.
Whether fundraising picks up again after $25bn this quarter versus $43bn a year ago.
Global Atlantic insurance earnings, which fell this quarter.
